newsitem.title: USA: Celtrix starts Phase II burn trial.
newsitem.headline: Celtrix starts Phase II burn trial.

text.p: Celtrix Pharmaceuticals Inc announced on Tuesday it has begun a Phase II clinical feasibility study for the systemic treatment of severe burns using SomatoKine.
The company said in a statement the trial is Celtrix's second Phase II feasibility study with SomatoKine. In January, it initiated clinical feasibility testing for recovery from hip fracture surgery.
"Our primary objectives in the burn study are to speed the patients' recovery time and reduce their hospital stay," said Dr Andreas Sommer, president and chief executive officer.

The company said its researh indicates that low blood levels of a vital anabolic hormone, IGF-I, may contribute significantly to a patient's difficulty in recovering from burns and that supplementation of the hormone may restore healthy metabolic processes required for healing.

SomatoKine is the recombinant equivalent of the naturally occurring complex formed in the bloodstream by IGF-I and its major binding protein, BP3. The company said it believes the compound can be used as therapy for about 8,000 people annually who suffer from severe burns in the U.S.
The study is expected to be completed during the first half of 1998.
